reason: Inherited immunoglobulin dysregulation supports infectious_immune; supplied evidence establishes no additional organ involvement. Low confidence is appropriate.
Cardiomyopathy, lactic acidosis and skeletal muscle dysfunction define the syndrome. Frequent myopathy supports musculoskeletal rather than inferring neurologic disease from hypotonia.

Lysosomal storage and neurodegeneration support both primary axes. Rod-cone dystrophy in 5/5 supports ocular involvement; vascular deposits without dysfunction do not support cardiovascular involvement.
Leukemia defines haematologic disease. Common hepatic infiltration and cutaneous leukemic occupation support involved hepatic and dermatologic axes; medium confidence reflects variable frequencies.

Microcephaly and developmental impairment define neurologic disease. Thyroid hormone deficiency in 2/5 supports endocrine involvement; antibody positivity alone does not establish an additional immune axis.

Organic aciduria and progressive neurodegeneration define the primary axes. Frequent strabismus and structural vertebral abnormalities support ocular and musculoskeletal involvement; isolated cardiac reporting is insufficient.
Defining contractures support musculoskeletal disease. Short stature and hypotonia alone establish neither endocrine nor neurologic involvement; sparse evidence warrants low confidence.
Renal dysplasia, encephalocele and polydactyly define the classic syndrome. Common hepatic ductal plate malformation with fibrosis supports hepatic involvement, reaching the four-axis cap.

Intellectual disability and renal anomalies define the syndrome. Frequent persistent neutropenia and sensorineural hearing impairment support the involved axes; omitting camptodactyly under the cap is reasonable.

Oxidative phosphorylation deficiency defines metabolic disease. Hepatic steatosis with biochemical injury and muscle abnormalities with hypotonia each affect 1/2; respiratory distress alone does not establish pulmonary damage.
